deep.reconstruction:
Context: this sheet continues the axiomatics of Newtonian gravitation from fol. 119v and is a draft of the fragment published posthumously in Riemann's Werke (1876) as 'Gravitation und Licht' / 'Neue mathematische Principien der Naturphilosophie'.

(A) Axioms, continued.
(2) Superposition: the force actually present at a point x is the vector (parallelogram) sum of the forces that would be present there if each ponderable point were alone: g(x) = sum_i g_i(x).
From fol. 119v, a single point of mass m_i gives g_i(x) = -m_i (x - x_i)/|x - x_i|^3, i.e. directed toward the point and inverse-square.
(3) At every point and instant there is a cause that would give any ponderable point placed there a motion determined in direction and magnitude, the same for all points. A moving point combines this with the motion it already has, by the parallelogram rule: dv = v_old + g dt. Riemann means 'the same for all points'; the transcription's 'gegen alle Punkte' should be read so.
These causes therefore differ in magnitude and direction. Insofar as the motion they impart is taken as their measure (Newton's 'virium quantitas acceleratrix', Principia Def. VII), they are called accelerating forces. So g is an acceleration field, independent of the test mass.

(B) The new hypothesis.
Riemann seeks the cause of g(x,t) in the motion of a substance (aether, 'Stoff') that continuously fills all of infinite space.
The velocity w of this substance has the direction of the force and magnitude proportional to it: w = c g.
The words 'gleich (entgegengesetzt)' show he hesitated over the sign. With w parallel to g, the flow is toward the masses.
For a single ponderable point at rest, the substance therefore streams in from all sides: w = -c m r_hat/r^2.
He states it is 'easy to show' that in such a motion the same quantity of substance always occupies the same volume (incompressibility). In modern terms (mine):
- div(r_vec/r^3) = 0 for r ≠ 0.
- Equivalently, the flux through every sphere about the point is 4 pi c m, independent of r.
The right-column cylinder argument makes this concrete. Take a cylinder with base dA perpendicular to the flow and height dh along it. During the inflow:
- the base shrinks like r^2;
- the height, by the velocity gradient dw/dr = 2cm/r^3, grows so that dh ∝ r^-2.
The volume dA·dh is therefore conserved. Hence 'dasselbe physische Raumelement nimmt stets denselben (geometrischen) Raum ein'.
This physical space ('physischer Raum') moves within geometric space.
Since the ponderable point's properties must not change, substance must continually vanish into it, at a rate proportional to its attracting power: d(volume)/dt = 4 pi c m. The point is a sink of strength ∝ mass, repeated on fol. 120v.

(C) Light and radiant heat in empty space must likewise be motions of this same substance. The known properties of these motions are:
- they are vibrations transverse to the direction of propagation;
- all of them propagate with the same speed.
To explain them, Riemann postulates internal forces of the substance. Each physical line element strives to expand or contract with a definite force, and this tension/pressure is the sum of two terms:
- the first depends on the extension or contraction the physical line element has previously undergone (an elastic, shear-type term);
- the second on the dilatation the volume element has previously undergone.
This is effectively a linear elastic medium with two moduli; transverse waves come from the shear term. Fol. 120v continues: these forces combine by the principle of virtual velocities.
errors: The sign hesitation 'gleich (entgegengesetzt)' is left unresolved. With the force directed toward the mass, flow velocity parallel to force means inflow, which is consistent with the sink picture that follows.
'Läßt sich leicht zeigen' (incompressibility) is asserted without proof on this page. It is correct (div of r/r^3 = 0 off the source; superposition extends it to many points).

The link between flow velocity and the acceleration of a test body is purely postulated. No dynamical mechanism is given for why a body in a streaming medium acquires acceleration equal to (a multiple of) the local flow velocity. This is a physical gap, not a mathematical error.
The draft is heavily cancelled and some sentences are grammatically incomplete. Example: 'zur Erklärung dieser ... anzunehmen' and the subsequent struck lines.

results.what: Superposition of gravitational accelerations and the definition of accelerative force as a field independent of test mass
results.modern_name: Gravitational field superposition / Newton's quantitas acceleratrix

results.what: Gravitational field identified with the velocity field of an incompressible space-filling aether flowing into masses, which act as sinks with strength proportional to mass
results.modern_name: Aether sink/flow theory of gravitation (analogue of Gauss law: div g = 0 outside sources)
results.usually_credited_to: Speculations by Euler, Challis, later Bjerknes, Yarkovsky; Riemann's version is published in Werke 1876 ('Gravitation und Licht')

results.what: Volume conservation of the cylinder element in radial 1/r^2 inflow (base ∝ r^2, height ∝ r^-2)
Aether stress as the sum of a term from line-element extension and a term from volume dilatation, to yield transverse light waves of a single speed
results.modern_name: Two-parameter isotropic linear elasticity (shear and bulk moduli) / elastic-solid aether

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of Riemann's well-known posthumously published fragment 'Gravitation und Licht' (Werke 1876). The aether-sink model of gravity and the two-term stress law for light are already attributed to him and widely discussed.

checkable.asserts: Divergence of r_vec/r^3 is zero away from the origin, so the inflow is incompressible (result 0).
Volume flux through any sphere of radius R is 4*pi*c*m, independent of R, so the sink strength is proportional to mass.
The height element along radial flow w=-k/r^2 evolves as dδ/dr = w'(r)δ/w(r) = -2δ/r, giving δ ∝ r^-2.
Base area ∝ r^2 times height ∝ r^-2 is constant: the cylinder's volume is conserved.

transcription_corrections: 'sucht ich nun' should read 'suche ich nun'.

'Diese Ursachen müssten sich also nach Größe und Richtung unterscheiden und ferner die Bewegung' should probably read '... unterscheiden. Insofern die Bewegung, welche sie jedem einzelnen ponderabeln Punkte ertheilen würden, als ihr Maß betrachtet wird, heißen sie beschleunigende Kräfte'.
In axiom 3, 'gegen alle Punkte' is likely 'für alle Punkte (gleiche)', i.e. the same motion for every ponderable point.

'daß er ihn beständig in gleichem ... seiner Anziehungskraft proportionalem Maße verschwinden' should read roughly 'daß in ihm beständig Stoff in gleichen Zeiten in seiner Anziehungskraft proportionalem Maße verschwinde'.

Right column: 'einen Cylinder, dessen Druck ein Flächenelement' is probably 'dessen Basis ein Flächenelement senkrecht auf die Richtung der Kraft, dessen Höhe ein Linienelement in der Richtung der Kraft ist'.
Right column: 'so ändert sich ... Höhe nach seiner Länge' is probably 'so ändert sich bei dieser Bewegung seine Höhe umgekehrt wie seine Basis'.

'Er nimmt also denselben physischen Raumelement stets denselben [gewaltigen] Raum ein' should read 'Es nimmt also dasselbe physische Raumelement stets denselben (geometrischen) Raum ein'; the struck word is not 'gewaltigen'.
'Die Kraft {Größe Druck} ist die Summe zweier Glieder' is likely 'Die Größe dieses Drucks ist die Summe zweier Glieder'.
The marginal 'Bewegungen in dem von ponderabeln Körpern freien Raum' is a heading; 'Körper' is struck and replaced by 'Körpern freien Raum'.
